commits: 5d0b8f2f fix(chat): let a stored attachment be removed, and clean up what nobody kept
8c165132 test(chat): keep the attachment-lifecycle probe that found the quota dead end

why.reported_as: 保留数据 + 一些微小的问题 (preserve the data, and fix the smaller problems)
why.found_by: scripts/probe_chat_workspace.py, a probe that drives the real endpoints through a session and prints what happens
why.defect: the 100 MB attachment allowance was a one-way door. Quota is measured in stored bytes and NOTHING released them: DELETE /api/agent/attachments/{id} did not exist (404), no screen listed a user's uploads, and a user who reached the ceiling received 400 ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_LIMIT on every later upload with nothing to act on. Deleting a conversation did not release the bytes its attachments held either.
why.second_defect: a draft the user abandoned (uploaded, never sent) stayed stored forever while being invisible, and the composer's remove button only dropped it from local state, leaving the bytes behind.

what_changed: DELETE /api/agent/attachments/{id} frees one of the caller's own attachments. The row survives (name, mime, kind, sha256 are what a historical message renders) while payload and extracted text are dropped, and metadata now reports removed:true with an empty url so the UI can say what happened instead of linking to a 404. Downloading a freed file answers 410 ATTACHMENT_REMOVED, not 409.
Deleting a conversation releases the bytes its own messages had sent, and returns attachments_released. History rows are untouched: only the byte count is freed.
An upload older than 24 h that no message references is reclaimed when the allowance is next exhausted, so a full account recovers without the user having to find something to delete.
The send path skips an attachment it cannot resolve instead of failing the turn: a draft whose file was deleted before sending must not become an error.

The composer's remove button now calls the API and keeps the card as 已移除/Removed; the send button ignores removed files; a full allowance reports storage rather than advising the user to check the file format; an oversize file names the limit it hit.
The build script's mirror guard compared a fixed 8-character slice, so a 7-character short SHA was rejected; it now compares over the length the caller supplied.
The rollback script hard-coded one build directory and now derives the compose context from the pin file name, falling back to the newest complete build directory.
The release-verification script cleans up agent_attachments for its disposable account, which the first run left behind.

scheduler.state: waiting out the previous holder's pg:lock:scheduler TTL, as designed
scheduler.note: same behaviour as the previous promote and as documented in the earlier manifest: the lock TTL (LOCK_HOLDER_TTL_SECONDS = 900) outlives the container that held it, so the new scheduler restarts until the key expires and then takes over on its own. The worker — which runs the actual scheduled tasks — starts immediately.

verified_this_release.public_routes: https://api.puregamma.ai/health 200; https://app.puregamma.ai/zh 200; https://app.puregamma.ai/zh/chat redirects an anonymous visitor (307); https://api.puregamma.ai/api/agent/workspace-capabilities 401 unauthenticated.

predictable_side_effect.scheduler: after every promote the scheduler restart-loops for up to 15 minutes while the previous holder's Redis lock TTL runs out; it then acquires the lock by itself (verified twice: the lock value became this container's own hostname:pid and stayed renewed). Nothing to do, but a release report should say so instead of discovering it.

follow_ups_not_shipped: the API rate limiter keys on the peer address it sees, which in production is the Caddy container rather than the visitor, so API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=120 and EXPENSIVE_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=20 are effectively per-deployment budgets. Writes (uploads, agent runs) therefore share a 20/min ceiling across all users. Pre-existing; surfaced because acceptance runs make bursts of uploads and correctly receive 429. Needs a trusted client address forwarded from Caddy.
the X login / DM bot work is still uncommitted and undeployed by design (see the earlier manifest's not_shipped_on_purpose).

rollback.database: not rolled back and not affected: no schema change in this release.
rollback.residual_risk: rolling back to 15f7b9d5 removes the ability to delete an attachment, so the allowance becomes a one-way door again and any file already freed stays freed; rolling back to 044effcf additionally removes the attachment feature itself, leaving stored files unreachable until the new image returns. Nothing is deleted by a rollback.
